answers.answer: In the 3-player case, the tied leaders gain nothing, while the player alone in last place pays 1 coin. In a 2-player unequal Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Census: a tied lead gives no coin; a unique last player pays 1; in a 2-player game the last player never pays.

answers.answer: You do not have to draw six. You may draw up to the allowance, but free Market spaces limit you to two draws here. Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers: draw any number up to the Knights Track allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but cannot execute it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall is the one-space exception). You may save a fully activated action for a later round. When executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays on its spaces.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Planning and Actions: fill gradually; activate only when all required spaces are occupied; an activation can be saved; after execution, Followers return to the bag and Technology stays.

answers.answer: Starting with the Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly, taking one activated action or passing on each turn. Passing ends your participation for that Action Phase, so you cannot act again that round. Unused activations retain their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Actions: take one activated action or pass; passing ends participation; unused activations keep their Followers on the board.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances your Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Farm House: put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.

answers.answer: Village recruits one of a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader, placing the recruit in your bag and advancing that profession's track one space. Boatman gives the depicted coins, except the first player reaching its last space gets a Citizen instead. Craftsman gives a Technology tile, which can be used only after you pass. Trader gives a Place Tile: the first track advance allows category I only, and later advances allow I or II.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: put the chosen neutral Follower into your bag and advance its profession track; each profession's distinct reward is listed there.

answers.answer: No. A newly acquired Technology is used only after you pass, so it cannot help execute another action this round after that pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Each Technology permanently fills one action space; later ones may replace any profession except Monk. Do not place more than one at a Place or any at a Place requiring only one Follower; Technology cannot be moved once placed.
answers.evidence: Technology: first placed Technology must replace a Farmer; later ones may replace any profession except Monk; placement limits and permanence are stated. Craftsman-acquired tile is used only after passing.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only. Every later advance permits category I or II. Players may inspect both stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment and Setup: first Traders Track advance permits category I only; later advances allow I or II; players may inspect the stacks at any time.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and gives its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track; that track sets future draw allowance. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. The fourth Knight does not increase the allowance above 7 at that step; the first player there may receive its Citizen. Once a character track reaches its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table and Character-track limits: University, Castle, Monastery effects; fourth Knight keeps allowance 7; once on a track's last space, the corresponding action cannot be taken again.

answers.answer: Yes, a Monk may replace a Knight for an ordinary action. No, a Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. No, a Monk cannot replace an exact profession required on Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Monks: a Monk can replace any other profession on ordinary actions, but no other Follower or Technology can replace a required Monk. Town Hall: Deeds require exact professions and substitutions cannot replace them.

answers.answer: One Ship or Wagon action moves your Merchant along exactly one adjacent Waterway or Road, respectively. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if several are there. An empty connection is legal and yields no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: one connection per action, at most one good, and empty Roads/Waterways are legal and yield no good.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building: Guildhall requires your Merchant in the town; a town with any player's station cannot receive another; Orléans allows one per player.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gains 1 Development Point by moving one space on the Development Track. When movement lands on or passes a coin space, collect its depicted coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen. On reaching or passing a Development Status space, Status immediately becomes its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium; Scoring: coin and Citizen spaces reward movement onto/past them, and Development Status changes immediately on reaching/passing its space.

answers.answer: Town Hall works with one or two Followers in a single action. Your four marked starting Followers cannot be used. Send one or both neutral Followers to free Deed spaces matching their exact professions; they may go to different Deeds. Each placement gives the depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization gives a choice of 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player filling a Deed's last space takes its Citizen, and sent Followers stay there for the game.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: one or both Followers, starting Followers prohibited, exact matching Deed spaces, listed rewards, and Citizen for filling the last space.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during that round's Action Phase, and it applies before the Event Phase. Other events are resolved in Phase 6. The first round opens with Pilgrimage because that tile is placed on top of the Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hour Glass and Event; Setup: round 1 always has Pilgrimage.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine qualify as food; wool does not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay food, you owe 5 coins instead; with fewer than five coins, pay the coins you have and undergo torture for each missing coin.
answers.evidence: Events, Harvest: pay one grain, cheese, or wine to the Goods Market; if unable, pay 5 coins; inability to pay those coins causes torture for the shortfall. Wool and brocade are not food.

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar is lost from your bag and returned to its game-board supply, making it recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. The colored starting Trader is kept, so no Follower is lost and no replacement draw is required. Marked starting Followers are not redrawn or lost to Plague.
answers.evidence: Events, Plague: neutral Follower returns to supply without moving its track marker; if a marked starting Follower is drawn, keep it and do not redraw.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin and cover the two-coin shortfall with any mix of eligible items: a built or unbuilt Trading Station; a random eligible neutral Follower from your bag (redraw marked starting Followers until eligible); a Development Point moved one space left but never onto or past a coin space; or a Goods, Place, or Technology tile. Sacrificed items are removed from the game. Marked starting Followers always stay with you and cannot be surrendered.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy): pay available coins and replace each missing coin with a listed item; starting Followers are excluded; items are removed from the game.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods Tile, even if another part of the action would still give a reward. The action becomes available again as soon as the required tile is available, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply is short, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies: unavailable-tile actions cannot be played; they become available when stock returns; insufficient common coins prevent receiving coins at that moment.

answers.answer: A tie for most built Trading Stations means nobody takes the set-aside bonus Citizen. Goods score grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, and brocade 5 points each. Built Trading Stations and collected Citizens score (stations + Citizens) multiplied by final Development Status. Equal final scores go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, the players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: unique most stations receives the set-aside Citizen; scoring table gives goods values and the stations/Citizens formula; tie-break goes by Development Track, then shared victory.
